messages:
nora: Hey team, new hire here (day 2). Running macOS Ventura on an M1 Air. Trying to get a local dev flow that matches infra: asdf for node/python, brew for tooling. Two weird problems: 1) when I run services in Docker (devcontainer) the containerized app can't reach the ssh agent for checking out private repos during build (git clone fails). 2) my local zsh dotfiles add a fancy prompt and some aliases that seem to leak into containers and break entrypoints. Anyone have a concise checklist for making host SSH forwarding + clean container envs work?
raj: Welcome! For SSH agent: forward SSH_AUTH_SOCK into the container. If using Docker Desktop on mac, enable "SSH agent forwarding" in the devcontainer.json or use a mount: 

"mounts": ["source=${env:SSH_AUTH_SOCK},target=/ssh-agent,type=bind,consistency=cached"],
"remoteEnv": {"SSH_AUTH_SOCK":"/ssh-agent"}

Then ensure the container has socat or openssh-client to talk to the socket.

ellaine: Also if you're building images (docker build) and need private repos during build, use BuildKit's SSH forwarding: `DOCKER_BUILDKIT=1 docker build --ssh default .` and a Dockerfile line: `# syntax = docker/dockerfile:1.2` and `RUN --mount=type=ssh git clone git@github.com:org/private.git`. Don't bake host dotfiles into the image.
nora: I'm using VS Code devcontainer (remote container). I tried mounting SSH_AUTH_SOCK and setting remoteEnv but git clone during image build still fails. I think the build step runs as root before the mount exists?
raj: Right, mounts are available at container runtime, not all during build. For build-time private clone use BuildKit SSH as elaine said. For runtime clones (after container starts), mount socket and set SSH_AUTH_SOCK as above. For CI we typically use deploy keys or ephemeral tokens.
nora: Got it. About dotfiles leaking: my host zsh theme defines `ll` and a funky PS1 that mangles the container prompt. I usually bind my dotfiles into the container for convenience. How do you keep host dotfiles but prevent breaking container startup scripts?
ellaine: We recommend a minimal dotfiles subset for containers. In dotfiles repo we have `dotfiles/.container` which excludes interactive-only stuff. In your devcontainer.json, mount that path instead of the full dotfiles. Example: `mounts": ["source=${localWorkspaceFolder}/dotfiles/.container,target=/home/dev/.config,destination-type=bind"]`. Also use `if` guards in your shell rc, e.g.:

```
# in ~/.zshrc
if [ -z "$IN_CONTAINER" ] ; then
  source $HOME/.dotfiles/interactive.sh
fi
```

set `IN_CONTAINER=1` in devcontainer `remoteEnv` to skip those bits.
raj: Another small tip: clear interactive-only aliases for non-interactive shells: in your Powerlevel-like prompt setup wrap heavy code with `if [[ $- == *i* ]]; then ... fi`. That prevents scripts and entrypoints from choking on functions that expect a tty.
nora: Nice. Any mac M1/Brew weirdness I should watch for? I installed some formulae under /opt/homebrew but some build scripts expect /usr/local. Also serial-key signing tool we use is x86-only.
ellaine: On Apple Silicon, prefer /opt/homebrew. If a tool requires x86, install Rosetta and run needed binaries under arch -x86_64, but prefer to avoid that for devflow. For signing hardware tokens, reach out to security for a compatible agent or an alternative signing workflow.
ci-bot: Note: CI policy requires builds not to rely on host SSH sockets. Use deploy keys or build secrets for reproducible builds.
nora: Thanks! Quick follow-ups: 1) where do I request Rosetta install approval? 2) who owns the canonical `.container` dotfiles for devcontainers?
ops-bot: For Rosetta approval, file infra ticket IT-5342 and tag `security-approval`. For canonical container dotfiles, see repo `infra/dev-environments/dotfiles/.container` and ping @elaine for PR review.
nora: Awesome, I'll open the ticket and make a small `.container` PR. One last oddball: after fixing mounts, `ssh-add -l` inside the container shows my keys but `git clone` still prompts for passphrase. Should I run `ssh-add -K`?
raj: Don't use `-K` (mac keychain). If keys are protected by passphrase, ensure agent on host has unlocked the key before forwarding. `ssh-add -l` shows the key but if agent can't prompt for passphrase the agent won't add it. Best is to `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_ed25519` on the host once at login, or use a `ssh-agent` with key loaded automatically via keychain integration.
nora: Loaded the key on host and now container clones fine. Thanks for the rapid help everyone! :tada:
